name: Independent on Sunday cryptic crossword No 1,378

clue.text: Too many gluttons ask for seconds

indicators.note: asking for seconds here means taking the second letter of each word in turn

blocks.note: second letters of the three words
second letter of this word too

explanation.surface: A dig at greedy diners who always want a second helping.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words mean as well or in addition, interchangeable as adverbs in a sentence.

clue.text: Endlessly dry region on the easternmost tip of California?

definitions.text: Endlessly dry region on the easternmost tip of California?

indicators.note: without an end, so each of the next two words loses its final letter
in an across-reading word the east is the right-hand end, so the last letter is kept

blocks.note: a synonym, cut short by the indicator

explanation.surface: A geography question about the arid land on California's eastern border.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue doubles as the definition: the desert state lies on California's eastern edge, and its name is built from the truncated words plus the last letter of California.
explanation.definitionFit: The US state is largely desert and borders California to the east, so the full description fits it.

clue.text: Temporary name given to a strong drink

blocks.note: a short is a small measure of spirits
a term is a name for something

explanation.surface: Someone christens a stiff drink with a fleeting nickname.
explanation.walkthrough: A short is British pub talk for a measure of spirits such as whisky, as opposed to a long drink.
explanation.definitionFit: Something lasting only a brief period is temporary, an adjective pair with matching sense.

clue.text: Praise God in recital

indicators.note: a recital is a spoken performance, so we hear the word rather than read it

blocks.note: the Lord is God; in a non-rhotic British accent the two words sound the same

explanation.surface: Worshippers praising God by reciting a prayer together.
explanation.definitionFit: To laud someone is to extol or glorify them, a formal verb for praising.

clue.text: Provide a university friend with news every 12 months

indicators.note: to provide something with an item is to fit it in, so the second group is placed inside the first

blocks.note: read as the plural of N, the abbreviation for new: two Ns

explanation.surface: Keeping a college friend up to date with the latest news once a year.
explanation.walkthrough: Treating news as several Ns, like pp for pages, is a playful setter's liberty.
explanation.definitionFit: Something done annually happens once a year, which is the same as once in each twelve-month span.

clue.text: Russian country house resembled a château, in part

indicators.note: only a portion of the words is taken, so the letters sit inside the phrase

blocks.note: found across the end of the first word, the article and the start of the third

explanation.surface: A grand Russian country home looked rather like a French castle.
explanation.definitionFit: A dacha is the traditional second home or villa in the Russian countryside.

clue.text: Feeling low, start to drink

indicators.note: the start of a word is its opening letter, which is all that is kept

blocks.note: to low is to make the sound of cattle

explanation.surface: Someone feeling down decides to begin drinking.
explanation.walkthrough: Low looks like the adjective for sadness, but here it is the verb for a cow's call.
explanation.definitionFit: A mood is an emotional state or temper, so a noun for a feeling.

clue.text: Famous explorer ought to lead a group heading north

indicators.note: in a down entry going north means reading upwards, back to front

blocks.note: ought is an old spelling of nought, zero

explanation.surface: A noted explorer should head a party going towards the Arctic.
explanation.walkthrough: Captain Lawrence Oates died on Scott's Antarctic expedition of 1912. Ought for zero is an old usage some solvers will not know.
explanation.definitionFit: Captain Lawrence Oates was a member of Scott's doomed polar expedition, remembered for walking out into the blizzard.

clue.text: Having difficulty following the German action film

indicators.note: a word that follows comes after, so the piece for having difficulty is sent second

explanation.surface: Struggling to follow a German-language blockbuster.
explanation.definitionFit: The 1988 Bruce Willis thriller set in a skyscraper is a classic of the action movie genre.

clue.text: The last word of a Japanese soup recipe is missing

indicators.note: something missing has been taken away, so a letter is dropped

blocks.note: R is the abbreviation for recipe, as on prescriptions

explanation.surface: A cook complains that the final instruction of a noodle-soup recipe has vanished.
explanation.walkthrough: R for recipe comes from the Latin recipe, take, written on prescriptions. The definition hides at the start in plain sight.
explanation.definitionFit: The word said at the close of a prayer is literally the final word, and also means a final agreement.

clue.text: Sticking around and dawdling

blocks.note: c is short for circa, around

explanation.surface: Hanging about and loitering instead of moving on.
explanation.walkthrough: Sticking around looks like one phrase, but the definition is just the first word. To clag is a northern British word for sticking or clogging.
explanation.definitionFit: Clag is a regional British verb meaning to clog or adhere, so the participle matches a word for adhering.

clue.text: How you may view parts of female long-distance triathlon?

linkWords: How you may view parts of

blocks.note: split the word: its first two letters are Fe, the chemical symbol for iron
the rest of the word is male, a man

explanation.surface: A question about how to watch the women's race in an endurance triathlon.
explanation.walkthrough: Viewing the word as two parts, Fe plus male, gives a chemical element and a man.
explanation.definitionFit: The branded endurance race combines a long swim, a cycle ride and a full marathon run.

clue.text: Shortened many pretty skirts - this could be one of them

definitions.text: this could be one of them

indicators.note: to skirt something is to go round its edge, so one word encloses the other

explanation.surface: Lots of pretty skirts have been hemmed shorter.
explanation.walkthrough: Shortened describes the garment: it is a pair of shortened trousers cut to look like a skirt, so it could be one of the skirts.
explanation.definitionFit: These are knee-length divided garments that hang like a skirt, so one could count among the skirts.

clue.text: Frequently went for shelled nuts

indicators.note: a shelled nut has lost its outer casing, so the outermost letters go
nuts means crazy, so the remaining letters are scrambled

explanation.surface: Someone regularly chose nuts with their shells removed.
explanation.walkthrough: Went for reads as chose, but it is just the letters; shelled strips the first and last of the phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are adverbs meaning many times or regularly, interchangeable in a sentence.

clue.text: Supplying alcoholics with assorted ales and gin shows a complete lack of feeling

indicators.note: assorted means mixed up, so these letters are jumbled
to supply one group with something is to put that thing inside it

blocks.note: the letters of the two drinks

explanation.surface: Plying recovering drinkers with beer and spirits is shockingly callous.
explanation.walkthrough: A complete lack of feeling reads as heartlessness in the surface, but medically it is loss of the sense of pain.
explanation.definitionFit: The medical term means absence of pain sensation, which is a total numbness to feeling.

clue.text: Flexible, fit American guys in the lead

explanation.surface: Athletic American men up front are supple.
explanation.walkthrough: In the lead puts the American and the guys before the word for fit.
explanation.definitionFit: An amenable person is willing to go along with things, accommodating rather than rigid.

clue.text: It's moved around in a lorry with great skill

definitions.note: the answer is an adjective; the phrase works adjectivally, as in a person with great skill

indicators.note: things moved around are rearranged, so the letters change order
one piece is placed inside the other

blocks.note: an artic is an articulated lorry

explanation.surface: Something being driven about in a truck, handled very deftly.
explanation.walkthrough: A lorry is the British word for a truck, and an artic is one with a separate tractor and trailer.
explanation.definitionFit: Being artistic means having creative talent or flair, showing skill in the arts.

clue.text: Made up a story about a newspaper getting stolen

indicators.note: about means around, so one piece wraps the other

explanation.surface: A journalist invented a tale about a paper being pinched.
explanation.walkthrough: The FT is the Financial Times, the British business daily.
explanation.definitionFit: To lift something is informal for taking it without permission, so the past participle means pinched.

clue.text: Time with kinky porn star is ecstasy

indicators.note: kinky means twisted, so the letters are bent into a new order

explanation.surface: A cheeky claim that time spent with an adult film actor is bliss.
explanation.walkthrough: Ecstasy is not the drug here but a rapture.
explanation.definitionFit: A transport of joy is an overwhelming emotion, a rapture or state of bliss.

clue.text: British novel about the end of one chap's relationship with another

indicators.note: the end of a word is its final letter, which is all that is kept

blocks.note: roman is French for a novel, used in English too

explanation.surface: A British book telling how one man's friendship with another ends.
explanation.walkthrough: About is not a link but the abbreviation c for circa. Roman as a word for a novel appears in roman à clef.
explanation.definitionFit: The modern word describes a close, non-sexual friendship between two men.

clue.text: Meteor exploding far in the distance

indicators.note: an explosion scatters pieces, so the letters are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: A shooting star bursts apart high up and a long way off.
explanation.definitionFit: Something remote is distant or far away, an adjective of the same sense.

clue.text: Fast hit by a karate expert

blocks.note: a dan is a black-belt grade in martial arts

explanation.surface: Someone struck quickly by a martial artist.
explanation.walkthrough: Fast looks like an adjective for speed but is the noun for going without food.
explanation.definitionFit: The Islamic holy month is observed by daytime abstinence from eating and drinking.

clue.text: A person who boasts about good fashion knowledge

indicators.note: turning about means facing the other way, so the letters run backwards

blocks.note: garb is a style of dress

explanation.surface: A show-off who keeps telling everyone how much they know about style.
explanation.walkthrough: Boasts about reads as one phrase, but about belongs to the wordplay. Art here is skill or knowledge, as in the art of cooking.
explanation.definitionFit: A braggart is a loud show-off who constantly brags, so a noun for someone who boasts.

clue.text: Rocky terrain footwear

indicators.note: rocky means unsteady, so the letters are shaken into another order

explanation.surface: Shoes suited to stony ground.
explanation.walkthrough: A trainer is the British name for a sports shoe or sneaker.
explanation.definitionFit: A trainer is a soft sports shoe, so an item of footwear.

clue.text: McDonald's start ordering more salt, resulting in confusion

indicators.note: the start of a name is its opening letter
putting things in order rearranges them, so these letters are reshuffled

explanation.surface: Customers at a burger chain asking for extra salt cause chaos.
explanation.walkthrough: Ordering looks like placing a food order, but it is the instruction to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: A maelstrom is a whirlpool, and figuratively a state of turbulent chaos and turmoil.

clue.text: A big mountain - one in East Germany

indicators.note: one piece placed inside another

blocks.note: E for East and GER for Germany

explanation.surface: A tall peak said to be found in the former GDR.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface invites a mountain in the old East Germany; the peak is actually in the Swiss Alps.
explanation.definitionFit: The Eiger is a famous Swiss Alpine peak known for its deadly north face.

clue.text: Artist has that fabric

blocks.note: an old word for that, as in yon hill

explanation.surface: A painter owns that particular cloth.
explanation.walkthrough: RA stands for Royal Academician, a member of London's Royal Academy of Arts.
explanation.definitionFit: Rayon is a synthetic textile made from cellulose, so a type of cloth.

clue.text: Former amateur Italian chefs may cook with it

definitions.text: Italian chefs may cook with it

explanation.surface: A one-time amateur cook in an Italian kitchen.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is descriptive rather than a synonym: it names a staple ingredient.
explanation.definitionFit: Spaghetti, penne and other such noodles are staple ingredients in Italian cooking.

clue.text: Man listening to salacious stuff

indicators.note: listening means the word is heard rather than read

blocks.note: pornography, which in a non-rhotic accent sounds like the answer

explanation.surface: A man caught listening to something smutty.
explanation.walkthrough: Man is a chess piece here, not a person.
explanation.definitionFit: Chess pieces are called men, and the humblest piece on the board is a foot soldier.

clue.text: An important person lacking the first signs of any real self-worth

indicators.note: the first sign of a word is its opening letter
lacking something means being without it, so letters are removed

explanation.surface: A VIP who has no true self-respect at all.
explanation.definitionFit: Dignity is a sense of pride and self-respect, the feeling of one's own value.

clue.text: Doctor Brown following a nurse about to deliver a baby

indicators.note: to doctor something is to tamper with it, so these letters are altered
turned about means the letters face the other way
following means coming after, so the doctored name is placed behind the nurse

explanation.surface: A medic called Brown, assisted by a nurse, is about to deliver a child.
explanation.walkthrough: Doctor Brown reads as a person's title, but the doctor is the instruction. EN is an Enrolled Nurse, a British qualification.
explanation.definitionFit: A newborn is an infant that has just arrived into the world.

clue.text: Japanese seaweed is flipping smooth

indicators.note: flipping something over turns it the other way, so the letters run backwards

blocks.note: to iron is to smooth out creases

explanation.surface: An exclamation that the seaweed is jolly smooth.
explanation.walkthrough: Flipping looks like a mild British expletive, as in flipping marvellous, but it is the reversal signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Nori is the edible red algae pressed into sheets for wrapping sushi.

clue.text: Relatively speaking, Liam Gallagher's least favourite part of December?

definitions.text: Relatively speaking, Liam Gallagher's least favourite part of December?

blocks.clueFragment: Relatively speaking, Liam Gallagher's least favourite
blocks.note: the surface reading: the Oasis singer's famously feuding older brother, a relative he dislikes
the setter's reading: the festive season, Christmas

explanation.walkthrough: Liam Gallagher of the band Oasis has long feuded with his songwriter brother, who shares a name with the French word for Christmas.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is both a carol word for Christmas and the first name of the Oasis guitarist brother.

clue.text: Porridge mix

blocks.note: first meaning: British slang for time spent in prison
second meaning: to blend with a spoon

explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests making oatmeal, but porridge is British slang for a prison sentence, and stir is slang for prison.
explanation.definitionFit: Both a slang term for jail time and a verb for blending ingredients by circular motion.
